title: Duke's velvet glove with an iron mitt
summary: Jones and Willard agree Duke disciplined subtly, as Procope put it, and the men stayed because they loved him.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: We were talking about Duke Ellington's discipline, and he said he's not a disciplinarian, but I think he was in many ways, don't you?
Yes. I think Russell Procope described it beautifully on the Today Show once. He said he handled the band with a velvet glove but an iron mitt under it. You know?
He was never doing something so ordinary as to make a rule and make everybody obey the rule, or --
Or fine somebody for being late.
He had a subtle, almost conniving way of getting what he wanted.
Yeah. But I believe that was one of the reasons those men stayed with him so long. There was a comfort about him. Because the guys loved him.
Did they love him, even the ones who Cootie and Johnny never got along with him, like (Inaudible) -- didn't seem need to get along with him. Never had a good word to say about him.
Well, they were all getting old by that
